children: Volvo Car is bracing for a slower shift to electric vehicles in the U.S. than in other markets, while adding a mix of hybrid and battery-powered cars to its overall model lineup.

"Electrification is not growing in U.S. right now," Volvo's Chief Commercial Officer Erik Severinson said in an interview. "We need to have a more pragmatic bridge to full electrification for the U.S."

Volvo in 2024 dropped its goal of selling only EVs by 2030, after consumers in some countries proved more reluctant to embrace the technology than it had assumed. The company has also been grappling with the fallout from U.S. tariffs and stiff competition in China.

The company said Thursday that it planned to roll out 13 new models by the end of the decade adapted to regional demand requirements--seven for Western markets and six for China--in a bid to revive sales growth.

Severinson said Volvo would decide in which Western markets it would launch the seven new cars depending on local customer preferences. The Western models will be made in Europe or the U.S., and the models for China in that country, Severinson said.

In the U.S., changes in tax policies and general consumer sentiment against EVs have hurt sales of purely electric cars, with big differences among states, Severinson said. The Trump administration stripped away tax incentives for buying them last year.

Nonchargeable hybrid cars will have a role to play for many years in the country's car market, while plug-in hybrids offer a transition technology for consumers hesitant to go fully electric, he added.
"I hardly have any customers going back to combustion-engine cars," Severinson said. "It seems to be a one-way street."

title: Volvo Car to Add Hybrid Models to Lineup as U.S. EV Shift Stalls — Interview
